scenes.tts: Is netrin a gradient spreading from the midline, or a path laid down along the way?
scenes.visual: Title card: Where Is the Netrin? The map with a shaded gradient from the floor plate and a dotted band along the pia. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Is netrin a gradient spreading from the midline, or a path laid down along the way?

scenes.tts: Return to the map: the floor plate at the bottom, the progenitors around the canal.
scenes.visual: The transverse spinal cord map: dorsal commissural neurons at top, floor plate at the ventral midline, ventricular zone around the central canal, pial surface at the outer edge, commissural path drawn from dorsal cord down near the pia, then in across the floor plate. The floor plate and the ventricular zone are highlighted.
scenes.narration: Return to the map: the floor plate at the bottom, the progenitors around the canal.

scenes.tts: Start in a dish. A growth cone compares the cue on its two sides.
scenes.visual: A bead in a gel releasing netrin; a growth cone some distance away, its two sides marked near and far.
scenes.narration: Start in a dish. A growth cone compares the cue on its two sides.

scenes.tts: Around a small source, like a bead, concentration falls with distance.
scenes.visual: A curve of concentration against distance, falling steeply near the bead. Formula on screen: C = k / r. Small label: ideal case, steady small source, no cue lost.
scenes.narration: Around a small source, like a bead, concentration falls with distance.

scenes.tts: The fractional difference across a growth cone is roughly its width over its distance from the source.
scenes.visual: Formula on screen: fractional difference ≈ w / r, with w and r marked on the drawing.
scenes.narration: The fractional difference across a growth cone is roughly its width over its distance from the source.

scenes.tts: Close in, a growth cone sees about a ten percent difference. A millimetre away, about one percent.
scenes.visual: Two growth cones, 10 µm wide: at 100 µm the bars differ by 10%; at 1 mm they differ by 1%.
scenes.narration: Close in, a growth cone sees about a ten percent difference. A millimetre away, about one percent.

scenes.tts: But a growth cone measures bound receptors, not netrin itself.
scenes.visual: A growth cone with receptors on each side; bound receptors lit, empty ones dark.
scenes.narration: But a growth cone measures bound receptors, not netrin itself.

scenes.tts: The K D is the concentration that fills half the receptors.
scenes.caption: The Kd is the concentration that fills half the receptors.
scenes.visual: A binding curve, fraction bound against concentration, with the half-way point marked Kd. Formula: C / (C + Kd).
scenes.narration: The Kd is the concentration that fills half the receptors.

scenes.tts: Give it the same ten percent difference at three backgrounds: far below the K D, at it, far above. Where is the bound difference largest?
scenes.caption: Give it the same ten percent difference at three backgrounds: far below the Kd, at it, far above. Where is the bound difference largest?
scenes.visual: Three points on the binding curve: a hundredth of Kd, Kd, a hundred times Kd. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Give it the same ten percent difference at three backgrounds: far below the Kd, at it, far above. Where is the bound difference largest?

scenes.tts: At the K D. Far below it, almost no receptors are bound on either side. Far above it, almost all are.
scenes.caption: At the Kd. Far below it, almost no receptors are bound on either side. Far above it, almost all are.
scenes.visual: Table on screen: 0.99% vs 1.09%; 50.0% vs 52.4%; 99.01% vs 99.10%. The middle row's difference, 2.4 points, is highlighted.
scenes.narration: At the Kd. Far below it, almost no receptors are bound on either side. Far above it, almost all are.

scenes.tts: Binding is noisy, because molecules arrive and leave at random. A tiny difference is easily lost.
scenes.visual: Receptors flicker between bound and empty; the small difference at low and high backgrounds vanishes in the flicker.
scenes.narration: Binding is noisy, because molecules arrive and leave at random. A tiny difference is easily lost.

scenes.tts: A fixed detector gets the most signal near its K D. Adapting, by resetting its baseline, lets the growth cone respond again as the background changes. It cannot remove the binding limit.
scenes.caption: A fixed detector gets the most signal near its Kd. Adapting, by resetting its baseline, lets the growth cone respond again as the background changes. It cannot remove the binding limit.
scenes.visual: The binding curve stays fixed, with the most sensitive band shaded around Kd. Beside it, a response trace jumps when the background rises, settles back to baseline, then responds to the next step. Labels: adaptation; Kd does not move.
scenes.narration: A fixed detector gets the most signal near its Kd. Adapting, by resetting its baseline, lets the growth cone respond again as the background changes. It cannot remove the binding limit.

scenes.tts: Now the embryo, where netrin one is made in two places.
scenes.caption: Now the embryo, where netrin-1 is made in two places.
scenes.visual: The transverse spinal cord map: dorsal commissural neurons at top, floor plate at the ventral midline, ventricular zone around the central canal, pial surface at the outer edge, commissural path drawn from dorsal cord down near the pia, then in across the floor plate. Two sources light up.
scenes.narration: Now the embryo, where netrin-1 is made in two places.

scenes.tts: Floor plate cells make it. So do progenitors across a broad stretch of the ventricular zone.
scenes.visual: Floor plate cells glow; progenitors across a broad ventricular-zone domain, ventral and intermediate, glow.
scenes.narration: Floor plate cells make it. So do progenitors across a broad stretch of the ventricular zone.

scenes.tts: The progenitors send netrin out along their fibres. It builds up at the pial surface, along the commissural axons' path.
scenes.visual: Netrin travels out along progenitor fibres and collects as a band at the pial surface, right along the commissural path.
scenes.narration: The progenitors send netrin out along their fibres. It builds up at the pial surface, along the commissural axons' path.

scenes.tts: So there are two candidate ways to guide. One is a gradient diffusing from the floor plate. That is chemotropism.
scenes.visual: A shaded gradient spreading from the floor plate. Labels: chemotropism; a model to test in the embryo.
scenes.narration: So there are two candidate ways to guide. One is a gradient diffusing from the floor plate. That is chemotropism.

scenes.tts: Guidance by netrin held on a surface is called haptotaxis.
scenes.visual: The netrin band on the pial surface, with a growth cone crawling along it. Labels: haptotaxis; a model to test in the embryo.
scenes.narration: Guidance by netrin held on a surface is called haptotaxis.

scenes.tts: In twenty seventeen, two groups deleted the netrin one gene from one source at a time, in mice. A conditional deletion removes a gene only in chosen cells.
scenes.caption: In 2017, two groups deleted the netrin-1 gene from one source at a time, in mice. A conditional deletion removes a gene only in chosen cells.
scenes.visual: Label: 2017. Two copies of the map: one with the floor plate source switched off, one with the progenitor source switched off.
scenes.narration: In 2017, two groups deleted the netrin-1 gene from one source at a time, in mice. A conditional deletion removes a gene only in chosen cells.

scenes.tts: If a floor plate gradient did most of the guiding, which deletion should cause more errors?
scenes.visual: The two maps side by side. Question on screen: which deletion hurts more?
scenes.narration: If a floor plate gradient did most of the guiding, which deletion should cause more errors?

scenes.tts: The floor plate deletion should. It did not. Without floor plate netrin, most commissural axons stayed on course.
scenes.visual: Floor plate deletion map: most commissural axons follow the normal path to the midline.
scenes.narration: The floor plate deletion should. It did not. Without floor plate netrin, most commissural axons stayed on course.

scenes.tts: Without progenitor netrin, many commissural axons went off course. A third study found the same pattern in the hindbrain.
scenes.visual: Progenitor deletion map: many axons wander off the path. A hindbrain inset shows the same pattern.
scenes.narration: Without progenitor netrin, many commissural axons went off course. A third study found the same pattern in the hindbrain.

scenes.tts: A deletion shows which source the axons need, not how they read it. A path and a short-range gradient both fit.
scenes.visual: Two drawings beside the result: a netrin path along the pia, and a short gradient near it. Both get a tick.
scenes.narration: A deletion shows which source the axons need, not how they read it. A path and a short-range gradient both fit.

scenes.tts: Nor is the floor plate idle. In the spinal cord, later studies found that its netrin still contributes.
scenes.visual: The floor plate source returns at partial strength alongside the progenitor source. Labels: 2019; spinal cord.
scenes.narration: Nor is the floor plate idle. In the spinal cord, later studies found that its netrin still contributes.

scenes.tts: So, much of the netrin that matters seems to act near where progenitors lay it down. That holds in the mouse spinal cord and hindbrain. In the spinal cord, the floor plate keeps a part.
scenes.visual: Box 3 on the map fills, line one: much of the netrin acts near where progenitors lay it down. Scope tag: mouse spinal cord and hindbrain. Line two, separate: the floor plate keeps a part. Scope tag: mouse spinal cord.
scenes.narration: So, much of the netrin that matters seems to act near where progenitors lay it down. That holds in the mouse spinal cord and hindbrain. In the spinal cord, the floor plate keeps a part.

scenes.tts: After crossing, the axons do not turn back. What changes in the reader is the next lesson.
scenes.visual: An axon crosses the floor plate and continues on the far side. Label: next, crossing the midline.
scenes.narration: After crossing, the axons do not turn back. What changes in the reader is the next lesson.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: netrin marks a place, and the growth cone decides what to do there.
scenes.visual: The transverse spinal cord map: dorsal commissural neurons at top, floor plate at the ventral midline, ventricular zone around the central canal, pial surface at the outer edge, commissural path drawn from dorsal cord down near the pia, then in across the floor plate. All three boxes filled. Takeaway on screen: netrin marks a place; the growth cone decides what to do there.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: netrin marks a place, and the growth cone decides what to do there.
